title: Multiplexer (MUX)
summary: A multiplexer selects one of 2^n inputs based on an n-bit select signal. A 2:1 MUX: output = (NOT sel AND A) OR (sel AND B). An n:1 MUX uses 2^n AND gates + 1 OR gate (or tree). MUXes are used for data selection, bus sharing, and implementing Boolean functions. A MUX with n select bits and 2^n data inputs is a universal logic element (can implement any 2^n-input Boolean function).

structure.meaning: Output = (NOT S AND A) OR (S AND B). 1 select bit chooses between A and B.
Output = D[S1,S0]. 2 select bits choose among D0-D3.
Output = D[S2,S1,S0]. 3 select bits choose among D0-D7.
General: n data inputs, log2(n) select bits.
Uses transmission gates (pass transistors) instead of AND/OR. Fewer transistors but no gain restoration.
A 2:1 MUX can implement any 2-input Boolean function by connecting constants or inputs to the data inputs.

notes: MUXes are used in ALUs (operation selection), memory (address decoding), and bus arbitration.
A MUX is the dual of a DEMUX (demultiplexer).
MUXes can implement any Boolean function (Shannon expansion).
Transmission gate MUXes are faster and smaller but lack gain.
MUX delay = O(log n) for tree-structured MUXes.
